Public 81 is PinMAME's generic upper-right flipper button position. Paragon has no separate upper button: its extra flippers share the lower buttons, the driver declares FLIP_SW(FLIP_L) only, the VPinMAME library writes this position only when the table configures an upper flipper solenoid (it does not), and holding it in play changed no output.

Public 82 is the right cabinet flipper button. Paragon's buttons are not in the switch matrix: the plug-connector sheet wires them to the solenoid driver (A3J2-1 R. FLIP SW.) so each switches its side's two flipper coils through the K1 flipper-enable relay. The driver declares FLIP_SW(FLIP_L) without FLIP_SOL, so PinMAME reads this position of its own flipper column and raises the right flipper output 46 while the button is held and the relay (19) is up; the ROM never reads it. In play, holding 82 raised 46, and after a tilt it raised nothing.

mechanisms.behavior: Paragon is a one-ball game with no trough: the ball drains into the outhole below the flippers, closing switch 8, and the outhole kicker (public 7) serves it to the shooter alley, where the player launches it with the plunger. The ROM adds the bonus when the ball enters the outhole, then kicks it; a credit with the ball in the outhole starts the game, kicks the ball and resets both drop-target banks in the same step.

mechanisms.behavior: Four drop targets standing one behind the other on the left wall, A (switch 4) at the front to D (switch 1) at the back; the ball can reach each only once the ones in front of it are down. Each target scores and advances the bonus; the third (C) awards the 2X multiplier and the fourth (D) the 3X. Completing the bank does not reset it: the Treasure Chamber saucer resets the targets on its second entry in a ball, and the ROM fires the shared reset coil (public 2) at game start and at each new ball. Option S22 lets each target spot a PARAGON letter.
mechanisms.label: Valley of Demons four in-line drop targets

mechanisms.behavior: Three drop targets on the right, C (switch 17) at the front to A (switch 19) at the rear, each scoring 500. Knocking all three down scores the lit value (10,000, 15,000, 20,000, 25,000, then special), advances the waterfall lane value, and makes the ROM fire the shared reset coil (public 17). The value is remembered from ball to ball.
mechanisms.label: Waterfall three-bank drop targets

mechanisms.behavior: An upper-left saucer at the end of a narrow lane: a clear plastic guide on the lane's left and a metal deadening piece on its right slow the ball so it drops in, and the saucer kicks it up towards the top of the playfield (public 8). It always scores 5,000; its first entry in a ball awards 5X, its second the same-player-shoots-again lite and resets the in-line targets, and once all four targets are down again it awards a special.
mechanisms.label: Treasure Chamber saucer

mechanisms.behavior: A top left-centre saucer that scores the lit golden cliffs value (2,000 up to 20,000), advances it one step, and kicks the ball out (public 9). The value is remembered from ball to ball; IPDB notes that each entry adds a note to a tune.
mechanisms.label: Golden Cliffs saucer

mechanisms.behavior: A top right saucer ringed by the seven PARAGON letters. Each entry spots the lit letter in the centre PARAGON row, scores and advances the bonus, and kicks the ball out (public 10). With all seven spotted the special lite lights; the next entry scores 25,000 and a special and resets the letters.
mechanisms.label: Paragon saucer

mechanisms.behavior: Three bumpers in the upper middle (left, right and centre) and one at the lower left above the Beast's Lair. Each skirt switch makes the ROM fire its own coil: 40 fires 11, 39 fires 12, 38 fires 13 and 37 fires 1.
mechanisms.label: Four thumper bumpers

mechanisms.behavior: The pair above the lower flippers: switch 36 makes the ROM fire the left slingshot (14) and switch 35 the right (15).
mechanisms.label: Two slingshots

mechanisms.behavior: A spinner on the left whose switch closes once per rotation. The manual says it advances the bonus; its four lamps (14, 30, 46, 62, bottom to top) sit in a column the art captions ADVANCE BONUS When LIT, and a closure in play lit lamp 14.
mechanisms.label: Spinner

mechanisms.behavior: Two lower flippers and two extra Paragon flippers: a small one on the left wall aimed at the Valley of Demons targets and one on the right above the lower right flipper aimed at the waterfall targets. Each button fires both flippers of its side. The K1 relay (public 19) switches the flipper circuits: it is raised from game start to game over and dropped by a tilt. European machines that shipped with three flippers lack the upper right flipper.
mechanisms.label: Four flippers

IPDB machine id 1755: Paragon, Bally Manufacturing Corporation, project date December 05, 1978, manufactured June 1979, model number 1167-E, MPU Bally AS-2518-35, 9,120 units, widebody; notable features 'Flippers (4), Pop bumpers (4), Slingshots (2), 4-in-line drop targets (1), 3-bank drop targets (1), Kick-out holes (3), Standup targets (2), Star rollovers (4), Spinning target (1)'; design Greg Kmiec, art Paul Faris. The notes record that an unknown quantity of machines shipped to Europe (reportedly all in France) had three flippers, with a ball guide and a single post replacing the upper right flipper and a mini-post added in the Beast's Lair. Retained as the Internet Archive capture https://web.archive.org/web/2024id_/https://www.ipdb.org/machine.cgi?id=1755.
